title: Relations among sets
competency: Describe relationships among sets: equal, equivalent, subset and proper subset.

keywords.def: Two sets with exactly the same elements. A = B.
Two sets with the same number of elements. A ↔ B.
A ⊆ B when every element of A is also in B.
A ⊂ B when A ⊆ B and B has at least one element that is not in A.
A drawing that shows sets as circles.

en.text: Two sets are equal when they have exactly the same elements. Order and repetition do not matter. {p, q, r, s} = {q, r, p, s}, and {1, 1, 2, 2, 3} = {1, 2, 3}.

screens.title: Same or different?
screens.ask: A = {p, q, r, s} and B = {q, r, p, s}. Are A and B the same set?
screens.after:
Both sets hold p, q, r and s.
Only the order is different.
Order does not matter in a set.
So A and B are the same set: A = B.

screens.title: A. Equal sets
paras: Definition 1.2: Two non-empty sets A and B are equal if they have exactly the same elements. We write A = B.

screens.title: Equal or not? Tap each pair.
items: A = {p, q, r, s}, B = {q, r, p, s}
Equal: same elements, different order. A = B.
Equal: repeats do not count. C = D.
Not equal: v ∉ F and 3 ∉ E.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Two sets with exactly the same elements. A = B.

screens.text: Equal sets? True or false: {2, a, 4} = {a, 2, 4}
screens.why:
First set: 2, a, 4.
Second set: a, 2, 4.
Every element is in both sets; only the order changed.
So the sets are equal. True.
screens.clue: Check each element. Does order matter?

screens.text: Equal sets? True or false: {m, a, c} = {a, m, d}
screens.why:
m and a are in both sets.
c is in the first set only.
d is in the second set only.
Not exactly the same elements, so not equal. False.
screens.clue: Is every element in both sets?

screens.why:
Repeats count once: {5, 5, 6} = {5, 6}.
The second set is {6, 5} = {5, 6}.
Same elements, so the sets are equal.
True.

screens.ask: Find the missing element: {4, x, 9} = {9, 7, 4}. So x = ___
screens.why:
Equal sets have exactly the same elements.
The second set holds 9, 7 and 4.
4 and 9 already appear in the first set.
The only element still missing is 7.
So x = 7. Check: {4, 7, 9} = {9, 7, 4}.
screens.clue: Which element of the second set is missing from the first?

en.text: Two sets are equivalent when they have the same number of elements. {5, 7, 9} and {x, y, z} both have 3 elements, so they are equivalent. Equal sets are always equivalent, but equivalent sets need not be equal.

screens.title: What is the same?
screens.ask: {5, 7, 9} and {x, y, z} share no element. What do they have in common?
screens.after:
{5, 7, 9} has 3 elements.
{x, y, z} also has 3 elements.
No element is shared, but the count is the same.
Sets with the same count are called equivalent.

screens.title: B. Equivalent sets
paras: Definition 1.3: Sets A and B are equivalent, written A ↔ B, if they have an equal number of elements.
screens.note: All equal sets are equivalent, but not all equivalent sets are equal.

screens.title: Count, then decide: equivalent or not? Tap each pair.
items: 3 and 3 elements: E ↔ F. Equivalent, but not equal.
A = {p, q, r, s}, B = {q, r, p}
3 and 3 elements: C ↔ D. They are also equal.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Two sets with the same number of elements. A ↔ B.

screens.text: Equivalent sets: which set is equivalent to {a, 3}?
screens.why:
Count the elements of {a, 3}: a and 3, so 2.
Count each option: { } has 0, {2, 3} has 2.
{a} has 1 and {3} has 1.
Only {2, 3} has 2 elements.
So {2, 3} ↔ {a, 3}. The elements need not match.

screens.text: Equivalent sets? True or false: {5, 7, 9} ↔ {x, y, z}
screens.why:
{5, 7, 9} has 3 elements.
{x, y, z} has 3 elements.
Same number of elements, so the sets are equivalent.
True.

screens.text: Equal or equivalent? True or false: all equivalent sets are equal sets.
screens.why:
Try {1, 2} and {a, b}.
Both have 2 elements, so {1, 2} ↔ {a, b}.
But their elements are different, so they are not equal.
One example is enough. False.

screens.title: Equal, equivalent or neither?
screens.why:
Step 1: count both sets. Same count means equivalent.
Step 2: compare the elements. Same elements means equal.
{1, 2, 3} and {3, 1, 2}; {p, q} and {q, p}: equal and equivalent.
{1, 2, 3} and {a, b, c}: 3 and 3, different elements: equivalent only.
{1, 2} and {1, 2, 3}: 2 and 3 elements: neither.
screens.clue: First count, then compare the elements.

screens.text: Equivalent but not equal: A = the whole numbers less than 4. Which set is equivalent to A but NOT equal to A?
screens.why:
Whole numbers start at 0: A = {0, 1, 2, 3}.
A has 4 elements.
{0, 1, 2, 3} and {3, 2, 1, 0} are equal to A.
{0, 1, 2} has only 3 elements.
{1, 2, 3, 4} has 4 elements, but 4 ∉ A.
So {1, 2, 3, 4} is equivalent to A, not equal.
screens.clue: Write A first. Then look for 4 elements that are not the same.

en.text: A is a subset of B, written A ⊆ B, when every element of A is also in B. The empty set is a subset of every set, and every set is a subset of itself. The subsets of {1, 2} are { }, {1}, {2} and {1, 2}.

screens.title: Inside another set
screens.ask: A = {2, 3, 5} and B = {2, 3, 5, 7, 9}. Is every element of A also in B?
screens.after:
Check each element of A in B.
2 ∈ B, 3 ∈ B, 5 ∈ B.
So every element of A is in B.
We say A is a subset of B.

screens.title: A inside B
screens.ask: Tap a circle, then tap each number.
rings: {2, 3, 5}: every element is also in B.
numbers: In A, so also in B.
In A, so also in B.

screens.title: C. Subsets
paras: Definition 1.4: A is a subset of B if every element of A is also an element of B. We write A ⊆ B.
A = {a, c, e} is not a subset of B = {a, e, i, o, u}, because c ∉ B. We write A ⊄ B.

screens.title: Note
paras: 1. The empty set is a subset of any set: { } ⊆ A.
2. Any set is a subset of itself: A ⊆ A.

screens.title: All subsets of {a, b, c}, by size

root.label: {a, b, c}
root.info: Sort its subsets by how many elements they keep. 1 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 8 subsets.

children.label: 3 elements
children.info: {a, b, c}: the set itself. 1 subset.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A ⊆ B when every element of A is also in B.

screens.why:
Check each element of {2, 6, 8} in {6, 8}.
6 ∈ {6, 8} and 8 ∈ {6, 8}.
But 2 ∉ {6, 8}.
One missing element is enough. False.
screens.clue: Check every element of the first set.

screens.why:
∅ has no element.
So no element of ∅ is missing from {2}.
The empty set is a subset of every set.
True.

screens.text: List the subsets: A = {0, b}. Tap every subset of A.
screens.why:
Size 0: { }.
Size 1: {0} and {b}.
Size 2: {0, b}, the set itself.
So A has 4 subsets.
{1} and {0, 1} are not subsets: 1 ∉ A.
screens.clue: Use no element, one element, then both.

screens.ask: How many subsets does {a, b, c} have? ___
screens.why:
List the subsets by size.
0 elements: { }. That is 1.
1 element: {a}, {b}, {c}. That is 3.
2 elements: {a, b}, {a, c}, {b, c}. That is 3.
3 elements: {a, b, c}. That is 1.
1 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 8 subsets.
screens.clue: List them by size: 0, 1, 2 and 3 elements.

en.text: A is a proper subset of B, written A ⊂ B, when A ⊆ B and B has at least one element that is not in A. A set is not a proper subset of itself. In a Venn diagram, a proper subset is a circle inside a bigger circle.

screens.title: Itself?
screens.ask: Is {a, c} a proper subset of {a, c}?
screens.after:
{a, c} is a subset of itself.
A proper subset must leave out at least one element.
{a, c} leaves nothing out of {a, c}.
So {a, c} is not a proper subset of itself.

screens.title: D. Proper subsets
paras: Definition 1.5: A is a proper subset of B, written A ⊂ B, if A ⊆ B and B has at least one more element.
A = {a, e, c} and B = {a, c, d, e}: every element of A is in B, and d is extra. So A ⊂ B.

screens.title: Note
paras: 1. The empty set is a proper subset of any other set: { } ⊂ A, if A is not empty.
2. No set is a proper subset of itself: A ⊄ A.
The proper subsets of {a, c} are {a}, {c} and ∅.

screens.title: Venn diagrams
paras: A Venn diagram shows a set as a circle. The elements go inside the circle.
A = {1, 4, 5} and B = {1, 4, 5, 6}. A ⊂ B, so circle A is drawn inside circle B. 6 is in B but outside A.

screens.title: A ⊂ B as a Venn diagram
numbers: Only in B: this makes A a proper subset.

screens.title: Not inside: A = {1, 2, 3}, B = {3, 4}
sets: Only in A: 1 and 2. So A ⊄ B.
Only in B: 4. So B ⊄ A.
overlaps: Only 3 is in both. The circles overlap; neither is inside the other.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A ⊂ B when A ⊆ B and B has at least one element not in A.
A drawing that shows sets as circles.

screens.why:
7 and 4 are both in {7, 4, 5, 6}, so {7, 4} ⊆ it.
The bigger set has extra elements: 5 and 6.
Subset plus something extra means proper subset.
True.
screens.clue: Is A inside B, with something left over?

screens.text: Proper subset? True or false: {a, b, c} ⊂ {c, a, b}
screens.why:
Both sets hold a, b and c.
So the sets are equal.
The second set has no extra element.
A set is not a proper subset of itself. False.
Note: {a, b, c} ⊆ {c, a, b} is true.
screens.clue: Does the second set have any extra element?

screens.text: List the proper subsets: B = {m, 2}. Tap every proper subset of B.
screens.why:
All subsets of B: { }, {m}, {2}, {m, 2}.
A proper subset must leave something out.
{m, 2} is B itself, so remove it.
Proper subsets: { }, {m}, {2}.
{m, 2, 0} is not even a subset: 0 ∉ B.
screens.clue: Proper subsets leave out at least one element.

screens.text: Choose the Venn diagram: M = {0, 4, 6, 8} and N = {6, 8}. Which Venn diagram is right?
opts: Two circles that do not touch
screens.why:
Check N in M: 6 ∈ M and 8 ∈ M.
So N ⊆ M, and M has extra 0 and 4. N ⊂ M.
A proper subset is drawn inside the bigger circle.
So circle N goes inside circle M.
0 and 4 sit in M, outside N.
screens.clue: Is every element of N in M?

screens.text: Subsets both ways: A ⊆ B and B ⊆ A. What must be true?
screens.why:
A ⊆ B: every element of A is in B.
B ⊆ A: every element of B is in A.
So neither set has an extra element.
They have exactly the same elements: A = B.
A ⊂ B is wrong: B has nothing extra.
screens.clue: If each set is inside the other, what can you say?

items.why:
Check each element: 1, 4, 3.
All three are in {3, 4, 1}.
So the first set is a subset of the second.
True. (The sets are in fact equal.)

6 and 8 are in {6, 8}.
2 is not: 2 ∉ {6, 8}.
Every element must be in the second set.
False.

items.text: Exercise: proper subset? True or false: {a, b, c} ⊂ {c, a, b}
items.why:
Both sets hold a, b, c, so they are equal.
The second set has no extra element.
A set is not a proper subset of itself.
False.

items.text: Exercise: proper subset? True or false: { } ⊂ {3, 4}
items.why:
{ } is a subset of every set.
{3, 4} has extra elements: 3 and 4.
So { } is a proper subset of {3, 4}.
True.

items.text: Exercise: let A = {0, b}. Tap every subset of A.
items.why:
Size 0: { }.
Size 1: {0} and {b}.
Size 2: {0, b}.
{0, 1} is not a subset: 1 ∉ A.
So A has 4 subsets.
items.clue: Include the empty set and A itself.

items.text: Exercise: choose the Venn diagram. E = {a, x, m, 4} and F = {a, 4, 8, 9}. Which Venn diagram fits?
opts: Two overlapping circles: a and 4 in the middle
Two circles that do not touch
items.ans: Two overlapping circles: a and 4 in the middle
items.why:
Find the shared elements: a and 4.
Only in E: x and m.
Only in F: 8 and 9.
Something shared, but neither set is inside the other.
So two overlapping circles, with a and 4 in the middle.
items.clue: Which elements are in both sets?

items.text: Exercise: true or false? All equal sets are equivalent.
items.why:
Equal sets have exactly the same elements.
So they have the same number of elements.
Same number means equivalent.
True.
items.clue: Same elements means the same count.

items.text: Exercise: true or false? A set is a proper subset of itself.
items.why:
A proper subset leaves out at least one element.
A leaves nothing out of A.
So A ⊆ A, but A ⊄ A as a proper subset.
False.

items.text: Exercise: true or false? If A = B, then A ⊆ B.
items.why:
A = B means they have the same elements.
So every element of A is in B.
That is the meaning of A ⊆ B.
True.
items.clue: Any set is a subset of itself.

test.why:
Both sets hold 1, 2 and 3.
Only the order is different.
Order does not matter in a set.
True.

test.text: Equivalent sets: which set is equivalent to {p, q, r}?
test.why:
{p, q, r} has 3 elements.
{1, 2} has 2, {p, q} has 2, { } has 0.
{4, 5, 6} has 3.
So {4, 5, 6} ↔ {p, q, r}.

3 ∈ {1, 3, 5, 7}.
5 ∈ {1, 3, 5, 7}.
Every element of {3, 5} is in the second set.
True.

test.text: Proper subsets: tap every proper subset of {x, y}.
test.why:
All subsets: { }, {x}, {y}, {x, y}.
{x, y} is the set itself.
A set is not a proper subset of itself.
Proper subsets: { }, {x}, {y}.

Subsets of {1, 2, 3} by size: 1 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 8.
The set itself, {1, 2, 3}, is not proper.
8 − 1 = 7 proper subsets.

notes.text: Example 2 prints {1,2,3, } with a stray comma; shown as {1, 2, 3}. Example 11 prints B = {a, c, d, e, }; shown as {a, c, d, e}.
Examples 3–4 print F = {x, , u, 3} (an empty slot). Read as F = {x, u, 3}, which Example 4 needs (3 elements). Teacher to confirm.
Example 13 writes ∅ ⊆ A in a list of proper subsets; it should be ∅ ⊂ A.
The Venn note on p.7 says A = {1, 5, 6} but the drawing shows 1, 3 and 2. Not used in the lesson.
Definition 1.5 says "B has at least one more element"; the lesson explains it as "an element that is not in A".
Venn diagrams with one circle inside another use the nest block; the student cannot draw circles, so Exercise 1.2.1 Q4–Q5 are asked as multiple choice.
